subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive & pricing qualification (FintechX)
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks for the call — FintechX / Redwood follow-up

Marissa and team,

Thanks for the walkthrough today — really helpful to see Redwood's serving options and the Dedicated/private deployment trade-offs. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can model this internally:

- Current use case: realtime personalization and content generation for transactional notifications + two experimental features (account summary generation, insights summarization).
- Expected ramp: pilot (Q1) ~10M tokens/month -> production (Q3) 80-120M tokens/month; heavy tail during promos.
- Primary concerns: inference cost / unit economics, SOC2 + data residency, and predictable SLAs for peak days.

Next steps we discussed:
1) You to share a simple unit-econ template showing cost per 1M tokens, recommended configs (batching/quantization), and $/feature breakdown.
2) Our procurement to get pricing ranges and an SOW for Dedicated if numbers look good.

Attaching high-level expected volumes internally (I'll share a spreadsheet if helpful). Also cc'ing Tom (platform) and procurement.

Appreciate it,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, FintechX
Alicia.gomez@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fintechx.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — FintechX / Redwood follow-up

Alicia — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the ramp expectations. I attached our unit-econ template (redwood_unit_econ_template.xlsx) and a short SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf) for procurement and security review.

To make the deep dive efficient, could you confirm the following so we can pre-populate the model?
- Preferred baseline model profile (throughput vs quality): latency-sensitive realtime vs high-quality batch. If unsure, we can model both.
- Target $/1M tokens you mentioned on the call (range is fine) or target monthly budget.
- Expected # of unique features that will call the model in production (we can map $/feature).
- CAC payback target / gross margin targets for the product (so we can show how inference cost impacts unit economics).

High-level framing we'll include in the template:
- Token cost (hosted) vs Dedicated amortized cost per 1M tokens (with common quantization/batching knobs).
- $/feature breakdown (avg tokens per request * requests/month).
- Impact on gross margin assuming various CAC payback windows.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill in the expected tokens per feature in the template and return prior to our deep-dive.
- Schedule 60-min unit-econ deep-dive next week (I left a Calendly link below).

Calendly: https://calendly.com/marissa-co/uec-deep-dive

If helpful, Neha can join to run through the recommended batching/quant settings for your workload.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tlee@fintechx.com>, procurement@fintechx.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — FintechX / Redwood follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the template and SOC2 summary. Quick answers below so you can pre-populate: 

- Baseline model profile: latency-sensitive for notifications (avg target p95 < 400ms), higher-quality for scheduled batch generation (account summaries). Please model both lines.
- Budget range: pilot budget roughly $3k–5k/mo; production target $22k–32k/mo (we expect to hit ~100M tokens/mo at scale).
- Features: 3 core features in prod (notifications, account summaries, insights); 2 experimental features for Q2.
- CAC payback: leadership is targeting 6–9 months payback on our AI-enabled product (hard constraint for pricing).
- Margin targets: gross margin contribution of at least 60% from the product line; want to see sensitivity to inference cost and host vs dedicated choices.

Also procurement asked for a sample SOW and an initial committed throughput SKU — can Neha route procurement SOW templates?

I'll try to fill the tokens-per-feature estimates into your sheet and send back by Monday. 

Best,
Alicia

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive & pricing qualification (FintechX)

Alicia — looping in SOW + procurement flow. Thanks for the budget ranges — that gives us a good baseline. Quick notes before the deep-dive:

- I'll prepare an initial pricing sketch: hosted (pay-as-you-go) vs Dedicated (committed capacity) with amortized $/1M token figures using your 100M/month projection. Expect a 20–40% delta depending on quantization/batching choices.
- For your CAC/margin targets (6–9mo payback, 60% gross margin), we'll model three scenarios: conservative (higher token consumption per request), expected (your estimates), and optimized (aggressive batching + int8 quant).
- Typical mapping we use in the template: requests/month * avg tokens/request -> tokens/month -> $/1M tokens -> $/feature/month -> contribution margin.

Neha will also attach a sample SOW for Dedicated SKUs and procurement next steps in a follow-up email to procurement@fintechx.com. Can you confirm who will own the PO on your side?

I'll be on the deep-dive next Tue at 10am PT unless you want a different slot.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fintechx.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tom Lee <tlee@fintechx.com>, procurement@fintechx.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive & pricing qualification (FintechX)

Alicia / team — great, thanks for the detail. Confirming next steps: 

1) We'll pre-populate the redwood_unit_econ_template.xlsx with a hosted vs Dedicated comparison using your 100M tokens/mo scenario and the two model profiles (latency-sensitive + batch).
2) Neha will send the sample SOW and a committed-throughput SKU proposal to procurement@fintechx.com by EOD Tuesday.
3) Deep-dive scheduled: Tue 17 Nov, 10:00am PT — calendar invite sent.

Quick asks for the template return (if you can):
- Avg tokens per request for each feature (notifications, account summaries, insights).
- Expected requests/month per feature (if you track event counts, a range is fine).
- Any compliance constraints (data residency / retention) so we can include cost of private deployment if needed.

If you prefer we can run a short sensitivity exercise during the call to show how $/1M tokens impacts $/feature and margin at different CAC payback windows. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
